classification.difficultyReason: Decompose each target input into an ordered sequence of graph transformations. The hardest part combines a translation, a horizontal stretch and a reflection, with the shift distance depending on the chosen order.

content.prompt: Describe a suitable sequence of transformations that can turn $f(x)$ into $g(x)$ below.

answer.short: Translate right by 6 units, then squash horizontally by a factor of 3.
answer.worked:
Translate right by 6 units to get $h(x)=\ln(x-6)$.

Squash horizontally by a factor of 3 by replacing $x$ with $3x$.

$$\begin{align*}g(x)&=h(3x)\\g(x)&=\ln(3x-6)\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Translate left by 3 units, then reflect across the $y$-axis.
answer.worked:
Translate left by 3 units to get $h(x)=\sqrt{x+3}$.

Reflect across the $y$-axis by replacing $x$ with $-x$.

$$\begin{align*}g(x)&=h(-x)\\g(x)&=\sqrt{3-x}\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Translate left by 2 units, then stretch horizontally by a factor of 3, then reflect across the $y$-axis.
answer.worked:
Translate left by 2 units to get $h(x)=\ln(x+2)$.

Stretch horizontally by a factor of 3 to get $k(x)=\ln\left(\frac{x}{3}+2\right)$.

Reflect across the $y$-axis by replacing $x$ with $-x$.

$$\begin{align*}g(x)&=k(-x)\\g(x)&=\ln\left(2-\frac{x}{3}\right)\end{align*}$$
